To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the time scales of the different degrees of freedom are essential for the understanding of the ordering phenomena and (b) the time scales can be inferred from the experimental data.

“the interplay of several electronic degrees of freedom close the instabilities of charge, spin and orbital order combined with the disparity between the time scales associated with their fluctuations can lead seemingly contradictory experimental findings.”
the time scale of fluctuations of a given degree of freedom can be used to determine its role in a given experimental measurement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed understanding of the electronic properties of solids and nanostructures.
the development of new theoretical methods and their application to the study of the electronic structure of complex materials.
the understanding of electronic and structural properties of solids, in particular of strongly correlated systems, by using first-principles many-body techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the time scales associated with different instabilities are not necessarily comparable.
the uncertainty principle is a fundamental concept in physics and that the time scales of the experimental probes have to be taken into account when interpreting experiments in solid-state systems.
the time scale of fluctuations is a key ingredient to understand the physics of many correlated materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quantum fluctuations are not just a nuisance, but a fundamental ingredient of solid-state physics.
we are now able to predict the time scales for different physical processes, and to relate the time scales with the experimental probes.
the time scale of fluctuations is an additional degree of freedom which can be exploited to understand the rich phase diagrams of solid-state systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time scale of fluctuations is a crucial ingredient for a proper interpretation of experimental results.
, for a given physical system, the time scale of an experimental probe can determine which degrees of freedom are observed in the experiment.
, when approaching a quantum critical point, the time scale of fluctuations is crucial to understand the nature of the ordering phenomena and their dynamics.
